requirements.evidence: Data model and contract are largely complete: slug binding (app/Models/Entity.php:20), memberships/users/owner relations (Entity.php:28-48), enum + manageable() (app/Models/UserRole.php:5-17), scopes/casts (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:20-70), named indexes and portable owner_seq (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000002_create_entity_memberships_table.php:19-23), policies (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:11-40, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:11-35), routes (routes/web.php:53-58), locked entityId (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:18-19) and audit log (app/Http/Controllers/EntityPickController.php:20-25). Edge case wrong: assignRole can target the owner's membership (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:90-95), breaking the exactly-one-owner invariant.

conventions.evidence: Policies, deliberate $fillable (app/Models/Entity.php:18, EntityMembership.php:20), reusable Blade components and docs/CHANGELOG updates are in place, but domain writes live directly in Livewire instead of app/Actions/* (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:41-119, Members.php:36-124) and validation bypasses the project's #[Validate] pattern (Members.php:46-49, Settings.php:47-50).

security.evidence: Actions re-authorize and inputs are validated/escaped (Settings.php:45,60,78; Members.php:40-44,79-83,111; Blade uses {{ }}), but app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:90-95 resolves any membership of the entity and writes its role without excluding the owner, so an admin can demote the owner and leave the entity with zero owners (the DB unique index only blocks a second owner).

tests.evidence: change.diff adds no files under tests/; none of the new models, enum, factories, policies, controller or Livewire actions ship a test, so there are no happy-path, unauthorized-call or tamper tests.

simplicity.evidence: Lean, no speculative abstractions, and it reuses existing x-form-field/x-button components; minor duplication: the entity is re-fetched on every render/action (app/Livewire/Entity/Dashboard.php:27, Members.php:126, Settings.php:124) and role checks are duplicated (Members.php:40-44 vs 79-83).

readability.evidence: Small focused methods and clear names (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:41-119, Members.php:36-124); small blemishes: unreachable defensive checks with a long comment (Settings.php:100-109) and duplicate unused lang keys (lang/en/ui.php:55-56,67-68).

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: models/migrations/policies/factories, entity pages, ui.* translations, routes, plus docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md; no unrelated refactors or out-of-scope features (no onboarding/switcher/navbar changes).

issues.explanation: assignRole() looks the membership up within the entity but does not exclude the owner's row, so an admin can set the owner's role to admin/employee; the DB unique index only forbids a second owner, so this leaves zero owners and permanently locks settings/transfer, and the view exposes the assign buttons on the owner row.
The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests at all, whereas the conventions require every feature/endpoint/action to be covered, including an unauthorized-call and a tamper test for each Livewire action.

All domain writes (save/delete/transfer, addMember/assignRole/removeMember) are implemented inline in the Livewire components instead of the required app/Actions/* classes (one per use case, authorizing inside the action).

Public input properties carry no #[Validate] attributes and validation is done via Validator::make / inline $this->validate() rules, deviating from the project's #[Validate] + $this->validate() pattern and Livewire rule 1.

addMember()/assignRole() authorize with hand-rolled membership role checks (and assignRole then also calls the policy), instead of authorizing solely through policies/gates as the conventions require; the manual checks duplicate and could drift from the policy.
owner_notice and transfer_property duplicate entity_owner_notice and transfer_ownership and are never referenced, leaving dead translation strings.
The locked entity is re-fetched from the database on every render/action via findOrFail; since the model property is #[Locked] and mount already authorized it, this adds redundant queries.
The target==owner and target user==caller checks are unreachable because the target is required to be an admin and the caller is the owner; the explanatory comment is misleading dead code.

review.summary: The change implements almost the whole entity data model, policies, pick endpoint and the Dashboard/Members/Settings pages with slug binding, locked server context and correct translation keys. It is not mergeable as-is: it lets an admin demote the owner through assignRole (breaking the single-owner invariant and bricking entity settings) and it ships zero tests, with further deviations around Actions and #[Validate].
